lead.headline: Democrats Win Both the House and the Senate in the US Midterms
lead.deck: A record number of ballots were cast, and Washington may now be split between two parties.
body: Midterm elections are held halfway through a US president’s four-year term. On 3 November, Democrats won control of the House of Representatives and the Senate. By early Wednesday they led the House 228 to 139, with several races undecided. AP reported a 54-44 Senate majority, also with two races undecided.
More than 124 million ballots were cast, according to the University of Florida Election Lab. That passes the previous midterm record of nearly 119 million in 2018.

The result ends Republican control of both houses of Congress. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer called it a “generational remake of the Senate map.” President Donald Trump said he has veto power, which lets him refuse to sign a bill, and that he would stay open to working with Congress.

world.headline: Ukraine, Russia and the US Sit Down in Abu Dhabi
world.deck: France says Europe will be there too, as the Kremlin had ruled it out.
body: Delegations from Ukraine, Russia and the United States meet in Abu Dhabi, in the United Arab Emirates, on Tuesday and Wednesday. It is the fourth round of talks led by the US and the first since February. Moscow agreed to return after US envoy Steve Witkoff met President Vladimir Putin in October.

France’s foreign minister, Jean-Noel Barrot, said Sunday that European officials will attend too and will make sure “Europe’s voice” is heard. The Kremlin’s spokesman, Dmitry Peskov, had said the three-way format was already agreed. Russia’s delegation, led by Vladimir Medinsky, now includes two deputy foreign ministers.

The two sides want different things. Russia wants Ukraine to give up large parts of its land and renounce NATO membership. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wants security commitments, including who would act if Russia attacked again. Russia also fired 36 ballistic missiles at the Kyiv area on Saturday, and Zelenskyy said four were intercepted.

us.headline: Trump Says His Immigration Crackdown Was “Too Tough”
us.deck: In a Sunday interview, the president said he is open to a deal on immigration.
body: In an interview on 60 Minutes on Sunday, President Donald Trump said his immigration enforcement was “too tough” and likely cost his party in the midterms. Immigration enforcement means checking who is allowed to live and work in the country.

He said he is open to a deal that would secure the border and let some immigrant workers stay if they have no criminal record and have lived in the United States for some time. He did not say when such a deal would happen. Any new law would need Congress to agree.
Trump also said voters “didn’t like the war” with Iran. On 6 November he said Stephen Miller will replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff.
us.why: Immigration affects workers, employers and families, so changes to the rules can reach many homes. It is a good topic for the table: what would a fair rule look like?

india.headline: India Offers 20 Blocks of Critical Minerals at Auction
india.deck: The ninth round also makes it easier to hold an auction.
body: Critical minerals are materials used in electric vehicles, renewable energy technology, defence equipment, aerospace, electronics and advanced manufacturing. On 5 November, India’s Ministry of Mines launched the ninth auction round in Goa.

It offers 20 blocks in Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan, Telangana, West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Bihar. The blocks hold minerals such as rare earth elements, vanadium, gallium, titanium, graphite, potash and glauconite.
In the first eight rounds, 64 of 100 blocks were successfully auctioned. Rules notified on 16 October cut the minimum number of qualified bidders in some rounds from three to two.

There are also 11 exploration blocks, aimed at copper, vanadium, rare earth elements and potash. An exploration licence lets private companies explore 29 critical and deep-seated minerals before mining begins. These blocks go to the bidder who quotes the lowest percentage of future mining revenue.
india.why: The minerals in this auction are used in electronics and electric vehicles, things many families use or plan to buy. Where they come from affects what they cost later.

lines.text: Good morning, and welcome to The Breakfast Table for November 10. Today we look at an election result in America, talks about the war in Ukraine, and what the US president said about immigration.
Let’s start with the election. What happened?

On November 3, Americans voted in midterm elections, which come halfway through a president’s four-year term. Democrats won control of the House and the Senate. In the early count they led the House 228 to 139, and AP reported a 54 to 44 Senate majority, with a few races still undecided.
Did a lot of people vote?

Yes. More than 124 million ballots were cast, passing the old midterm record of nearly 119 million from 2018. Representative Hakeem Jeffries, the Democratic leader, is in line to become Speaker of the House.
What does the president say?
President Donald Trump said he has veto power and would stay open to working with Congress. A veto means he can refuse to sign a bill into law.
Now to Ukraine.

Delegations from Ukraine, Russia and the United States meet in Abu Dhabi, in the United Arab Emirates, on Tuesday and Wednesday. It is the fourth round of talks led by the US, and the first since February.
Is anyone else joining?
France’s foreign minister said European officials will attend too, and that France will make sure Europe’s voice is heard. The Kremlin’s spokesman had said the three-way format was already agreed.
What are the two sides arguing about?

Russia wants Ukraine to give up large parts of its land and renounce NATO membership. President Zelenskyy wants security commitments, including who would act if Russia attacked again. Meanwhile, Russia fired 36 ballistic missiles at the Kyiv area on Saturday, and only four were shot down.
And the president’s interview?

In a Sunday interview on 60 Minutes, Trump said his immigration enforcement was too tough and likely cost his party in the midterms. He said he is open to a deal that would secure the border and let some immigrant workers stay if they have no criminal record.
Is that settled?
No. It is an idea he said he is open to, and Congress would have to agree to any deal. Trump also named Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff on November 6.
Which party won control of both the House and the Senate on 3 November?
Democrats Democrats won both houses of Congress.

That is all for today. Have a great day, and we will see you again tomorrow.
